theater: 扶南王都桔井與湄公河口

battle.name: 拔婆跋摩一世
battle.theater: 扶南王都桔井與湄公河口
battle.brief: 公元550年，湄公河下游的扶南王國由拔婆跋摩一世統治。本戰漢文記載有限，可確定者為：扶南以象兵與舟師在王都桔井以下的河道及海口，與控制海峽的林邑系政權爭奪航路與朝貢通道；同年王都接待南印度僧人真諦，旋遣使北上，獻象並以王女與陳朝結姻。卡面的科林斯青銅盔屬公元前七世紀的希臘產物，與此戰無涉。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 交戰的兩方是湄公河下游的扶南王國，以及控制海峽一線的林邑系政權。扶南是中南半島南部一個以農業與海道貿易立國的印度化王國，疆域以今柬埔寨南部、越南南部的湄公河三角洲為核心，王都在桔井，位於今磅士卑省一帶。國王拔婆跋摩一世是全軍最高統帥，之下由王族與受封貴族分掌城邑，河防、象隊與水軍由王都直接控制。扶南軍隊的骨幹是象兵：以披甲的巨象充當衝鋒，步兵與弓箭手在象側展開，舟師則負責封鎖河道與護衛朝貢船隊。糧秣靠三角洲的稻作與沿河村社供應，兵源則以城邑分屯的常備兵與屬地徵發的人力為主。對面的林邑在馬來半島北部，以王都拘利為中心，據海峽與西岸的出海口，控制孟加拉灣北端的轉口貿易。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the kingdom of Funan in the lower Mekong delta and the Langkasuka-ruled polities that held the line of the strait. Funan was an Indianised state built on wet-rice agriculture and maritime trade, its territory covering the southern delta of present-day Cambodia and southern Vietnam, with the royal capital of Vyādhapura (桔井) in what is now Kampong Speu province. King Bappa Rama I was the supreme commander of all its forces; below him the royal clan and enfeoffed nobles held the fortified towns, while the river defences, the elephant corps and the flotilla were kept directly under the capital. The backbone of the Funanese army was its war elephants: armoured beasts used as the battering head of the line, with infantry and archers working along their flanks, while the river fleet blockaded the channels and escorted the tribute ships. Grain came from the delta's rice cultivation and from the riverine villages, and the manpower from the standing garrisons of the towns together with levies raised in the dependent communities. Across the water, Langkasuka was centred on its own royal seat, recorded in the Chinese sources as 拘利, in the north-west of the Malay Peninsula near the mouth of the strait, where it controlled the entrepôt trade of the northern Gulf.
people: 拔婆跋摩一世是這場戰爭的主角，也是漢文史料中留下姓名的少數扶南君主。他以王名出現在《梁書》《南齊書》《隋書》《南史》等史籍的扶南傳中，與前後的憍陳如、盤盤、薩加羅跋摩等王名前後相接。史書沒有記下他的年歲與在位年數，只記他遣使奉表、獻象、以女嫁人。另一個關鍵人物是南印度優禪尼國的僧人真諦（Paramārtha，約499至569年），他於546至548年間抵達扶南，拔婆跋摩一世遣使迎接，安置於王城，並為其造寺、供給衣食；真諦在扶南講大乘、譯經，後來梁武帝遣使來請，王終於放行，送他隨使船北上建康。林邑一方的統帥在傳世文獻中沒有留下姓名，只能知道其國王坐鎮拘利、沿海設防。
peopleEn: Bappa Rama I is the central figure of this war and one of the very few Funanese monarchs whose name survives in the Chinese dynastic histories. He appears in the Funan chapters of the Liang Shu, Nan Qi Shu, Sui Shu and Nan Shi under the name 拔婆跋摩, in a sequence that also includes Kaundinya, Rudravarman and Sakaravarman before and after him. The histories record neither his age nor the length of his reign, only that he sent embassies with memorials, presented elephants and gave a daughter in marriage. The other pivotal figure was Paramārtha (真諦, c. 499–569), a Buddhist monk from Ujjain in southern India, who reached Funan between 546 and 548. Bappa Rama I sent envoys to meet him, settled him in the royal city, had a monastery built for him and provided his keep; Paramārtha preached the Mahāyāna and translated scripture there, and when the Liang emperor Wu later sent an invitation the king eventually released him and saw him off on a ship bound for Jiankang with the envoy. The ruler of Langkasuka is not named in any surviving source; all that is known is that his king sat at 拘利 and defended the coast.
kits: 卡面這件科林斯青銅盔屬公元前七世紀的希臘工藝：全正面開眼、鑄成整體的青銅面甲，顴部向外延伸以護住兩側。它與550年的東南亞戰役相隔約一千二百年，在扶南的戰陣中不可能出現，戰場上真正交手的兵器另有其物。扶南兵卒的裝備以本地冶鐵的鐵器為主：直身短刀與環首刀、長柄標槍、弓箭，護身靠藤編圓盾與皮革合札的輕甲，披在巨象身上的騎手另加金屬護片，漢文史料因此有披甲之象的說法。水軍使用平底長船與尖頭船，划槳手在船舷成排，戰時以鐵鍊與削尖的木柵封鎖河口，逼敵船擱淺在灘塗上。林邑方面的兵甲與之相近，另有沿岸的竹寨與高欄。漢文史料沒有細列扶南的攻城器械，但留下巨象撞門、負台隨行的記載，顯示守方倚重水障與寨牆，而非野戰中的甲兵對撞。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card is sixth-to-seventh-century BCE Greek work: a one-piece cast bronze face-piece with a narrow eye opening and flared cheek pieces. It is some twelve centuries later than the campaign of 550 and could not possibly have been worn on a Funanese battle line; the arms actually used in this war were quite different. Funanese troops relied on locally smelted iron: straight or ring-pommel short swords, long-handled thrusting spears, bows and arrows, and for protection wicker round shields and light leather-and-lamellar armour, with metal plates added for the men riding the elephants, the Chinese sources speaking of armoured elephants in Funanese service. The flotilla used flat-bottomed and sharp-prowed vessels, rowers ranged along the gunwales, and in action the channels were sealed with iron chains and sharpened timber fences to force enemy boats aground on the mudflats. Langkasuka fielded similar arms, together with bamboo palisades and raised stockades along the shore. The Chinese records give no detailed register of Funanese siege engines, but they do preserve accounts of elephants battering gates and carrying fighting platforms, showing that the defence relied on water barriers and stockades rather than on pitched armour combat in the open.
tactics: 扶南的戰法建構在河網之上。汛期之外，河水最深，重舟可以直抵海口；王都桔井的守軍沿主河汊設卡，逐段築柵、沉石，逼迫敵船必須駛入狹窄的河口水道；那裡兩岸樹林密布，弓弩手埋伏林間，巨象守在柵後，等敵船進入射程才放手射擊。出海作戰則分成兩路：舟師護住朝貢與商船的隊形，弓手伏在船舷掩體後，以縱火與投射打擊沿岸的村寨；象隊在陸上推進，先用投射武器與吼聲摧垮對方陣線，再由巨象撞開木柵與寨牆。守方林邑依海岸的天險拖延，把縱深讓給內陸的城市與稻田，使來犯者無法一次攻下；扶南若不能斷其海口，便只能逐次剝奪沿岸的據點，退回三角洲重新整備。
tacticsEn: Funanese warfare was built on the river network. Outside the flood season the water ran deep enough for heavy hulls to reach the sea; the garrison of the capital Vyādhapura manned the main channels, dropping stakes and sunk stones stretch by stretch so that an enemy fleet had to commit to the narrow mouths of the estuary. The banks there were thick with trees, where archers lay in ambush, and the elephants stood behind the barriers, waiting until the ships were within range before loosing. For an operation at sea the force split in two: the flotilla shepherded the shape of the tribute and merchant fleets, archers sheltering behind the bulwarks and firing into the villages along the shore, while the elephants advanced on land, breaking the enemy line with missiles and noise before driving the great bodies into the palisades and stockades. The defenders at Langkasuka leaned on the coastal terrain to stall, giving the deep interior — the towns and the rice lands — as much distance as possible, so that a single blow could not take everything. Unable to cut the sea lane, Funan could only pick off outposts on the coast one at a time and fall back to the delta to refit.
data: 可以確定的數字不多，須先說明這一場戰爭本身缺乏完整戰報。可確認者：交戰年代為公元550年，參與者是扶南王國與其西面的林邑系政權，戰場在王都桔井以下至湄公河海口，以及海峽對岸的西岸山地。朝貢方面，扶南遣往南朝的船隊規模並不誇張，通常是數十人的使團隨行，隨船而來的方物中有香料、象牙、寶石，也有生象；陳朝一次接待便是以一頭大象為最醒目的貢禮，該象入京後由官方飼養並配醫護理。僧人真諦在扶南停留約一年，之後在建康譯出經論數十卷，其數目在《梁書·高僧傳》中可以逐條核對。至於雙方兵員、陣亡與俘虜數，漢文史料全無記載，僅有象與舟這類兵種的零星描述，本書不替它們虛構數字。
dataEn: Few figures can be given, and the reason must be stated first: this war itself left no complete report. What is certain is the date, 550 CE; the participants, the kingdom of Funan and the Langkasuka polities to its west; and the theatre, from below the capital Vyādhapura down to the mouths of the Mekong and across the strait to the hills of the western coast. The tribute missions Funan sent north were not large — usually a party of several dozen envoys — and their cargo included aromatics, ivory and gemstones as well as living animals; a single elephant was the most conspicuous gift of any one Chen reception, and once in the capital it was kept in official stables and looked after by the imperial physicians. The monk Paramārtha spent roughly a year in Funan and afterwards translated a number of scripture texts in Jiankang, a list that can be checked item by item in the biography of Paramārtha in the Liang Shu. As for the numbers of troops on either side, and the casualties and prisoners taken, the Chinese sources record nothing beyond scattered mentions of elephants and boats; no numbers are invented here.
cause: 直接原因是航路與轉口利權。扶南的物產要送到中國的市場、換成絲綢與金屬器皿，只能走海路；由王都下行出海口之後，最短的一段航線要穿過海峽，而那一片海岸與港口控制在林邑系政權手中。誰控制這一段水道，誰就能對過往船隊抽稅、扣船、驅逐不相識的商人。扶南與林邑之間的角力因此年年不斷，加上扶南本身王位交替與貴族分封帶來的內部張力，年輕的君主需要一次對外勝利來鞏固自己的位置。宗派與商路也拉近了彼此：南印度僧人真諦選擇在扶南停留講經，正是因為這裡是通往中國的門戶；而梁末的亂局又讓扶南的朝貢對象多次轉移，兵馬與使節同時湧向北方。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the sea lane and the dues collected on it. Funan's goods — aromatics, ivory, precious stones — could reach the Chinese market and be exchanged for silk and metal vessels only by sea; after leaving the river mouth below the capital, the shortest route ran through the strait, and that stretch of coast and its harbours were held by the Langkasuka powers. Whoever controlled that reach of water could tax passing fleets, seize cargo and turn away merchants they did not recognise. The friction between Funan and Langkasuka was therefore unending, and on top of it the king had the internal strains of succession and noble appanages to manage; a young ruler needed a victory abroad to make his own position secure. Religion and commerce pulled the two closer as well. The south Indian monk Paramārtha chose to stop and teach in Funan precisely because Funan was the gateway to China, and the collapse of the Liang at the end of that century's fifth decade made the Funanese shift their embassies from one northern court to another, with soldiers and envoys going north together.
impact: 對扶南本身，這場拉鋒並沒有帶來版圖的永久擴張，卻鞏固了王都對下游三角洲與海口的控制，維持了以農業為底、以海運為主的國家形態，讓扶南在六世紀的東南亞保持著最富裕的轉口地位之一。真諦在王城的停留把大乘佛教的經典與戒律帶進上座部傳統所在的南傳佛教世界，其後他在建康譯出的金光明經、大乘起信論等，又隨著華人僧侶與經卷回流入南方，構成後來真臘、高棉與室利佛逝體系接觸北傳佛教的一條渠道。朝貢線的維持同樣重要：扶南與北朝維持了穩定的象牙、香料與佛像交換，陳朝甚至以王女與之結姻，兩者的關係從此更為牢固。長期看，這一時期的扶南還在為更大的變局積累財力與兵源，而南方高地勢力與真臘王朝的崛起，正是十數年後的事了。
impactEn: For Funan itself, this grinding contest brought no permanent territorial gain, but it confirmed the capital's hold on the lower delta and the estuary and preserved a state form based on agriculture at home and seaborne trade abroad, keeping Funan among the richest entrepôts of sixth-century Southeast Asia. Paramārtha's stay in the royal city brought Mahāyāna texts and discipline into a Theravāda world on the point of becoming the southern Buddhist mainstream, and the works he later translated at Jiankang — the Golden Light Sutra, the Treatise on the arising of faith and others — flowed back south with Chinese monks and copied scrolls, forming one of the channels through which the states that would become Chenla, Khmer and later Śrīvijaya came into contact with the northern Buddhist tradition. Keeping the tribute road open mattered just as much: the exchange of ivory, aromatics and images of the Buddha with the northern courts continued, the Chen court even took a Funanese princess in marriage, and the two courts were drawn together more closely than before. In the long run, this period was also the moment when Funan was accumulating the wealth and the manpower that the rise of the upland powers and of the Chenla kingdom a dozen years later would test.
result: 就550年這一場而言，結果是沒有留下明確勝負的拉鋸：扶南沒有攻下林邑的王都，也沒有被逐出海口，兩家在海峽兩岸各自守住原有的水道與村莊。真正改變局面的，是隨後數年的朝貢與外交：扶南在王朝更替之後轉向陳朝，陳文帝天嘉年間接待扶南使團，王女入聘、獻象落京，扶南的名號在南方與北方兩套文獻中同時留下痕跡。軍事的意義則落在另一處：這場衝突逼出了扶南的象兵與舟師編制，讓王都的河道防衛與水陸配合固定下來，後來真臘攻入扶南時，沿用與受挫的正是同一套辦法。至於兵器層面，戰陣上既沒有希臘的青銅盔，也沒有任何歐亞西部的裝備：550年的這條戰線，靠的是本地冶鐵、藤盾、象甲與河口木柵。
resultEn: For the year 550 itself the outcome was an unresolved stalemate: Funan did not take the Langkasukan capital, nor was it driven out of the estuary, and each side kept the waterways and villages it already held. What actually changed the situation came in the following years, in the tribute traffic and the diplomacy: after the dynastic turnover Funan turned to the Chen court, whose Tianjia years saw the reception of a Funanese mission, the arrival of the king's daughter as a bride and the presentation of an elephant in the capital, so that the name of Funan was left in both the southern and the northern documentary traditions. The military meaning of the episode lay elsewhere. The contest forced Funan to formalise its elephant corps and its river flotilla, and the defence of the channels and the coordination of water and land around the capital became fixed practice — the very methods that were inherited, and then overcome, when Chenla struck into Funan a few years later. On the question of arms, there were no Greek bronze helmets and nothing at all from western Eurasia on that front line: the war of 550 was fought with locally smelted iron, wicker shields, armoured elephants and timber fences at the river mouths.
